contents.reason: The canonical free-algebra presentation is a principal theorem of MA-4, where its split diagram and Beck's theorem are developed together rather than used before their definitions.

contents.reason: Split coequalizers are introduced at the opening of MA-4 because their absolute-colimit property and their role in Beck's theorem form that page's proof spine.

contents.reason: The absoluteness lemma is the engine for MA-4's construction of created coequalizers and would be disconnected machinery on the present monad-construction page.

contents.name: Example 5.4.7, the canonical algebra fork is split in the base but its splittings do not lift
contents.reason: This example explains precisely why Beck uses U-split pairs and is retained as a numbered bridge immediately after canonical presentations on MA-4.

contents.name: Definition 5.4.8, U-split coequalizers and ordinary versus strict creation
contents.reason: The three creation clauses are prerequisites for the ordinary and strict forms of Beck's theorem on MA-4 and are not needed for any MA-3 proof.

contents.name: Example 5.4.9, an adjunction counit gives a canonical U-split fork
contents.reason: The counit fork supplies MA-4's canonical-presentation proof and belongs with the U-split definition and Beck machinery rather than the two resolutions built here.

contents.name: Proposition 5.4.10, the Eilenberg–Moore forgetful functor strictly creates coequalizers of U-split pairs
contents.reason: Strict creation of U-split coequalizers is MA-4's key technical theorem and requires the split-coequalizer definitions deliberately postponed to that page.

contents.name: Corollary 5.4.11, monadic functors create U-split coequalizers and every object has a counit presentation
contents.reason: This corollary is the necessity half of Beck monadicity and is therefore proved on MA-4 after monadicity, U-split pairs, and canonical presentations are all available.

contents.name: Exercise 5.4.i, abelian-group coequalizers as cokernels and canonical presentations
contents.reason: The exercise specializes MA-4's canonical presentation to abelian groups; adding it here would require the very presentation theorem assigned to the next pair.

contents.name: Exercise 5.4.ii, direct proof and naturality of canonical algebra presentations
contents.reason: This is an alternate proof of MA-4's canonical-presentation theorem, so its diagram chase belongs in that theorem's contract rather than as a duplicate MA-3 result.

contents.name: Theorem 5.5.1, Beck's monadicity theorem
contents.reason: Beck's theorem is the landmark of MA-4 and depends on the complete split and U-split coequalizer development harvested from section 5.4.

contents.name: Corollary 5.5.3, standard algebraic categories are monadic over Set
contents.reason: The individual free monads and their algebras are identified here, while the stronger monadicity conclusions require Beck's criterion and are explicit MA-4 applications.

contents.name: Definition 5.5.4, finitary functor and finitary monad
contents.reason: Finitary monads depend on the filtered-colimit vocabulary and feed the algebra-cocompleteness theorem, both assigned to MA-4 rather than the basic monad page.

contents.name: Definition 5.5.5, category of models for an algebraic theory
contents.reason: Models of algebraic theories combine finitary monadicity with Lawvere-theory structure and belong to the later categorical-algebra development, not basic algebras for one monad.

contents.name: Corollary 5.5.6, compact Hausdorff spaces are monadic over Set
contents.reason: This is Manes' theorem, whose object and morphism directions and choice-sensitive compactness argument are the dedicated compact-Hausdorff block of MA-4.

contents.name: Example 5.5.7, extension-of-scalars, rings over abelian groups, diagram evaluation, and categories over quivers as monadic functors
contents.reason: These examples use tensor products, free rings, Kan extension for diagrams, or free categories on quivers; their monadicity applications belong after Beck on MA-4 or in those later subject tracks.

contents.name: Proposition 5.5.8, the reflexive tripleability theorem
contents.reason: The reflexive form is MA-4's practical monadicity criterion and needs reflexive pairs plus preservation of their coequalizers, concepts not used elsewhere on MA-3.

contents.name: Theorem 5.5.9, the contravariant power-set functor is monadic
contents.reason: MA-3 uses the power-set self-adjunction only to construct its induced double-power-set monad; proving the contravariant functor monadic requires the MA-4 tripleability machinery.

contents.name: Lemma 5.5.10, Beck–Chevalley for direct and inverse images in a pullback of monomorphisms
contents.reason: This lemma is a technical input to the preceding power-set monadicity theorem and is not needed for constructing the double-power-set monad on the examples page.

contents.name: Exercise 5.5.i, strict Beck monadicity
contents.reason: The strict theorem is a separate landmark on MA-4 because the library distinguishes equivalence-based monadicity from isomorphism-based strict monadicity.

contents.name: Exercise 5.5.ii, further algebraic categories monadic over Set
contents.reason: These are additional applications of Beck's theorem and are considered on MA-4 only after the criterion itself and the relevant algebraic free functors are available.

contents.name: Exercise 5.5.iii, proof of reflexive tripleability from Beck's theorem
contents.reason: The proof is the contract for MA-4's reflexive-tripleability proposition and cannot precede the Beck theorem from which it is derived.

contents.name: Exercise 5.5.iv, G-sets are monadic over Set

contents.name: Exercise 5.5.vi, monadic restriction functors between diagram categories
contents.reason: This general restriction result is a Kan-extension theorem for functor categories and belongs to the later Kan-extension block rather than the foundational monad page.
